reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive disorder of cholesterol biosynthesis caused by variants in DHCR7, encoding 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase, the final enzyme of the pathway
The biochemical hallmark is a raised concentration of 7-dehydrocholesterol with low or low-normal cholesterol
Characteristic malformations include microcephaly, distinctive facial features, cleft palate, and cardiac and genital anomalies
Syndactyly of the second and third toes (Y-shaped 2-3 toe syndactyly) is a classic and useful clinical clue
Ambiguous or undervirilised genitalia in genetic males reflects impaired steroidogenesis downstream of cholesterol
The clinical spectrum is wide, from mild learning and behavioural difficulties to severe multiple congenital anomalies incompatible with survival
Behavioural features overlapping with autism spectrum disorder are common
Dietary cholesterol supplementation is used, though its effect on neurodevelopmental outcome remains uncertain
reference.pathophysiology: 7-Dehydrocholesterol reductase catalyses the last step of cholesterol synthesis, reducing 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholesterol. In Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome this enzyme is deficient, so cholesterol production falls and the immediate precursor 7-dehydrocholesterol and its isomer accumulate. Cholesterol is essential for cell membranes, myelin, bile acids, steroid hormones and Sonic hedgehog signalling during embryogenesis. Deficiency during development therefore disrupts morphogenesis (explaining the malformation pattern, including holoprosencephaly-spectrum features from impaired hedgehog signalling), while accumulated precursor sterols may exert additional toxic effects. Impaired steroidogenesis contributes to the genital and adrenal manifestations.
additionalDifferentials: Trisomy 13 and other chromosomal malformation syndromes
Other inborn errors of cholesterol or sterol synthesis
Disorders of sexual development from other causes
CHARGE and other multiple congenital anomaly syndromes
additionalInvestigations: Plasma sterol analysis showing raised 7-dehydrocholesterol with low cholesterol
Echocardiography and renal ultrasound for structural anomalies
Assessment of genital anatomy and karyotype in undervirilised males
Brain imaging to identify midline and other malformations
redFlags: Multiple congenital anomalies with microcephaly and dysmorphism in a neonate
Ambiguous genitalia requiring urgent endocrine evaluation
Feeding difficulties, failure to thrive and recurrent illness
Signs of adrenal insufficiency during stress
reference.prognosis: Prognosis correlates with disease severity: the most severely affected infants have major malformations and high early mortality, whereas milder cases survive with variable intellectual disability and behavioural difficulties. Cholesterol supplementation may improve some physical parameters, but its benefit for cognition and behaviour is not clearly established.
pitfalls: Measuring only total cholesterol, which can be normal, rather than specific sterol profiling
Missing adrenal insufficiency during intercurrent illness or surgery
Attributing the phenotype to a chromosomal syndrome without sterol testing
Assuming cholesterol supplementation reliably improves neurodevelopment
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
management: Dietary cholesterol supplementation to raise cholesterol and lower precursor sterols, which may improve growth and some physical parameters.
Feeding support for poor feeding and failure to thrive, including nasogastric or gastrostomy feeding and management of gastro-oesophageal reflux.
Surgical correction of structural anomalies such as cleft palate, cardiac defects, genital anomalies and toe syndactyly where indicated.
Photoprotection against the characteristic cutaneous photosensitivity.
Monitor for and manage adrenal insufficiency, with corticosteroid stress cover during illness or surgery.
Surveillance of growth, development and plasma sterols, with developmental and behavioural intervention.
Coordinate care through metabolic medicine, clinical genetics and relevant surgical specialties.
Autosomal recessive inheritance, so offer genetic counselling, carrier testing and prenatal diagnosis to families.
